title: Daily Security Intelligence Briefing — October 24, 2026
summary: Active mass exploitation of core PHP2Shell vulnerabilities and widespread edge-device credential harvesting across enterprise firewalls demand immediate response (SecurityWeek, The Hacker News). Organizations must also prioritize massive patch rollouts from Oracle and HPE to protect underlying enterprise and network infrastructure.

tier1.title: 1. Mirai Botnet Joins Mass Exploitation of PHP2Shell Vulnerabilities

fields.label: Source & Article Link
fields.value: SecurityWeek

fields.label: Technical Severity / Domain
fields.value: Web Infrastructure / CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619 (Critical)

fields.label: Why You Must Read This
fields.value: Critical unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerabilities in the core PHP engine are undergoing active, automated mass exploitation by botnets including Mirai. Over five million servers globally running mod_php, PHP-FPM, and CGI configurations are exposed, with attackers actively deploying ASLR bypass techniques. Because Linux distributions often backport fixes without altering primary version strings, standard command-line checks can falsely indicate system safety.

fields.label: Recommended Immediate Action
fields.value: Audit PHP installations via package manager logs (e.g., dpkg/rpm) rather than runtime flags, upgrade to patched PHP releases (8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, or 8.5.12), and immediately restart web worker processes.

tier1.title: 2. Global Edge Infrastructure Campaign Exposes Over 70,000 Enterprise Credentials

fields.label: Source & Article Link
fields.value: The Hacker News

fields.label: Technical Severity / Domain
fields.value: Identity & Edge Security / Mass Perimeter Breach (Critical)

fields.label: Why You Must Read This
fields.value: A massive, coordinated threat campaign targeting exposed perimeter network appliances—specifically Fortinet FortiGate and Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect firewalls—has compromised over 70,000 credentials. Threat actors are utilizing harvested session tokens and administrative logins to establish initial access across thousands of organizations worldwide. Evidence indicates adversaries are already pivoting deeper into victim internal networks.

fields.label: Recommended Immediate Action
fields.value: Enforce mandatory password resets across edge access solutions, terminate all active VPN/firewall user sessions, mandate phishing-resistant MFA, and audit edge logs for anomalous secondary accounts.

tier2.title: 1. Oracle Patches 1,295 Flaws, Including Six CVSS 10.0 Vulnerabilities

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Enterprise Software

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Oracle released its October 2026 Critical Patch Update addressing 1,295 security vulnerabilities across its enterprise product landscape. Six bugs carry maximum CVSS 10.0 ratings, allowing unauthenticated attackers to achieve full takeover of core enterprise systems.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Flaws severely impact E-Business Suite, Access Manager, SOA Suite, PeopleSoft, and JD Edwards.; Unauthenticated exploitation via network access HTTP/HTTPS allows complete system takeover.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: This enables any unauthenticated attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise the workflow.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: CSO Online

tier2.title: 2. HPE ArubaOS Security Update Addresses 72 Flaws and Eight Max-Severity RCEs

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Wireless Infrastructure

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Hewlett Packard Enterprise released emergency security updates for ArubaOS to fix 72 vulnerabilities, including 33 critical flaws. Eight of these carry a CVSS 10.0 score, enabling unauthenticated remote code execution and authentication bypasses on enterprise wireless controllers.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Affects wireless infrastructure running ArubaOS AOS-8 and AOS-10.; Requires immediate firmware updates to AOS-10.8.1.2, 10.7.2.7, or corresponding fixed branches.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: 33 critical flaws that allow unauthenticated remote code execution and authentication bypass on wireless infrastructure.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: BleepingComputer

tier2.title: 3. CISA Adds Exploited Collabora Online and Arista VeloCloud Flaws to KEV Catalog

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Vulnerability Management

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: CISA has added CVE-2026-110447 in Collabora Online and CVE-2026-114625 in Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Both critical vulnerabilities allow unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code or SQL commands on host infrastructure.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: US Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies must apply mitigations by October 26, 2026.; Collabora flaw allows OS command injection when integrated within Nextcloud platforms.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Citing reports of active exploitation in the wild.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Hacker News

tier2.title: 4. Ruby Patches Onigmo Regex Memory Corruption Engine Underlying GitLab Flaws

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Application Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Ruby released updates for versions 4.0.9, 3.4.12, and 3.3.13 to resolve memory corruption flaws in its built-in regex engine, Onigmo. These vulnerabilities were identified as the root cause behind four critical remote code execution flaws recently patched in GitLab.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Applies to any Ruby application compiling user-supplied regular expressions.; Standard execution timeouts like Regexp.timeout fail to prevent the underlying memory corruption.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Any app compiling a Regexp from attacker input is exposed.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Hacker News

tier2.title: 5. LiteLLM Supply Chain Poisoning Distributes Cloud and API Key Stealer

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Supply Chain Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: LiteLLM version 1.107.0 was compromised on PyPI, Docker, and GHCR repositories following a release pipeline breach. Malicious code added to startup hooks executes on Python launch to harvest cloud environment tokens, SSH keys, and AI provider API credentials.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Injected code (`cook.pth`) triggers automatically upon any Python process initialization.; Exfils stolen credentials directly to encrypted endpoints under litellm[. ]dev.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Il codice applicativo non cambia: aggiunti solo cook.pth e due script... eseguiti a ogni avvio di Python.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: Mastodon (@trinacriatech)
